title: Tell a leak hunter which objects a collection would free

blocks.text: An operations team hunts memory leaks with a small tool that reads a heap dump: every object in the heap, the objects each one's fields refer to, and the GC roots (static fields and the local variables of live threads). Its report lists the objects the next collection would free. An engineer reads it to find what is holding the rest, so a report that names a held object as garbage, or a freed one as held, sends them after the wrong code.
`garbage(...)` already builds the report. Finish the `TODO` in `src/main/java/practice/HeapDump.java`:

items: `retained(heap, roots)`: the objects of the heap that a collection must keep.

cases.says: an object that no root refers to is reported as garbage, and the objects a root refers to are not
an object reached from a root through several references is kept
two objects that refer only to each other, with no root leading to them, are garbage
a cycle that a root leads to is kept, and the report still finishes

origin.section: An Object Lives While Something Reachable Refers to It

concepts: The collector keeps what it can reach from the GC roots; an unreachable cycle is collected, and anything a static field reaches is kept.
A static collection that only grows keeps every entry reachable, so the heap after collection grows until OutOfMemoryError.
